quote: Example 1. Let Xαi ∼ Burr(αi , βi , 2) (Xα∗i ∼ Burr(αi∗ , βi , 2)), for i = 1, 2, 3. Further, suppose that Ip1 , Ip2 , Ip3 (Ip∗1 , Ip∗2 , Ip∗3 ) is a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of the Xαi ’s (Xα∗i ’s), with E[Ipi ] = pi (E[Ip∗i ] = p∗i ), for i = 1, 2, 3. We take (α1 , α2 , α3 ) = (4, 0.7, 0.2), (α1∗ , α2∗ , α3∗ ) = (4.2, 0.6, 0.3), (β1 , β2 , β3 ) = (5, 3.5, 1.2), (p1 , p2 , p3 ) = (0.2, 0.3, 0.4), and (p∗1 , p∗2 , p∗3 ) = (0.25, 0.35, 0.25). It is clear that the conditions of Theorem 5 are satisfied. So, we have Y1:n∗ ≤hr Y1:n . Figure 1 represents the function rY1:n∗ (x) − rY1:n (x), which agrees with the intended result.

quote: Theorem 1. Let X1 , . . . , Xn (X1∗ , . . . , Xn∗ ) be independent and non-negative random variables with Xi ∼ r(x; αi , βi ) (Xi∗ ∼ r(x; αi∗ , βi )), i = 1, . . . , n. Further, suppose that Ip1 , . . . , Ipn (Ip∗1 , . . . , Ip∗n ) is a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of the Xi ’s (Xi∗ ’s), with E[Ipi ] = pi (E[Ip∗i ] = p∗i ), i = 1, . . . , n. Assume that the following conditions hold: (i) r(x; α, β) is increasing [decreasing] and convex in α for any β and any x > 0; (ii) ∂r(x;α,β)/∂α is decreasing (increasing) in β for any α and any x > 0. Then, for (α, β) ∈ Sn− (Sn+ ) and (α∗ , β) ∈ Sn− (Sn+ ), we have Πi=1..n p∗i ≤ Πi=1..n pi and (α1 , . . . , αn ) ⪯w [⪯^w](α1∗ , . . . , αn∗ ) =⇒ Y1:n∗ ≤hr Y1:n .
family: general two-parameter severity model: Xi has hazard rate r(x; αi, βi); claim amounts Yi = Ipi·Xi with Bernoulli(pi) indicators; Y1:n = smallest claim amount (portfolio minimum)
